Today’s Plan

P A R T  O N E
The Building Blocks
Four things every program today uses.
About 15 minutes

Two Rules for Today
Top to bottom
Python runs your lines in order, first to last, once each. 
Nothing is skipped and nothing repeats. That is what 
“sequential” means.
No if statements
Not even for the True/False problems. If you find 
yourself wanting one, you are looking for a Boolean 
expression instead — we will see exactly how.
Conditionals come later in the course. Today is about getting comfortable writing straight-line code.

input() Always Gives You Text
Even when the user types a number, Python hands you a string.
agesStr = input("How old are you? ")   # text
ages = int(agesStr)                    # a number
The naming convention we use all semester
1 Read the input into a name ending in Str.
2 Cast it to int or float.
3 Store the result under the same name, without the Str.
Why it matters
"5" + "3" gives 53, not 8. Text joins; numbers add. 
Forget to cast and your arithmetic silently goes 
wrong.
int or float?
• int — whole things you cannot have half of: 
people, days, guests.
• float — anything that can have a decimal: 
miles, gallons, degrees.

Three Kinds of Division
Slash, double slash, and percent do three different jobs.
/
True division
7 / 2  →  3.5
Always gives a decimal, even when it 
divides evenly.
//
Floor division
7 // 2  →  3
Throws away the remainder . How many 
whole times it fits.
%
Modulo
7 % 2  →  1
Gives only the remainder . The part left 
over.
Together they split a quantity up: 3725 seconds
3725 // 3600  =  1 hour
3725  % 3600  =  125 seconds left over
125 // 60    =  2 minutes,   125 % 60  =  5 seconds
Know these: 60 seconds in a minute, 3600 seconds in an hour .

Making Output Readable
print("") Prints a blank line — space out your output.
print("\n Title") The \n skips a line before the text.
print("\t Indented") The \t inserts a tab, so the line is indented.
round(value, 2) Rounds to two decimal places.
round(value) Rounds to the nearest whole number .
math.ceil and math.floor
You need these for the assignment.
import math
print(math.ceil(4.2))
print(math.floor(4.9))
ceil always rounds UP: 4.2 becomes 5.
floor always rounds DOWN: 4.9 becomes 4.
Neither cares which is nearer .

P A R T  T W O
Seven Programs
We write each one together . Type along.
About 30 minutes

Problem 1: Fahrenheit to Celsius
Convert a temperature the user types in.
# degreesC = (degreesF - 32) * 5/9
degreesFStr = input("Enter degrees Fahrenheit: ")
degreesF = float(degreesFStr)
degreesC = (degreesF - 32) * 5/9
print("Celsius degrees =", round(degreesC, 2))
Sample run
Enter degrees
Fahrenheit: 98.6
Celsius degrees = 37.0

Problem 2: Miles Per Gallon
Ask for miles driven and gallons used, then print a message with the answer.
milesStr = input("How many miles did you drive? ")
miles = float(milesStr)
 
galsUsedStr = input("How many gallons did you use? ")
galsUsed = float(galsUsedStr)
 
mpg = miles / galsUsed
print("You got", round(mpg, 2), "miles to the gallon")
Sample run
...miles did you drive? 300
...gallons did you use? 12
You got 25.0 miles
to the gallon

Problem 3: Is the Venue Within Capacity?
Print True or False — without an if statement.
capacityStr = input("Enter the venue capacity: ")
capacity = int(capacityStr)   # people, so int
 
guestsStr = input("How many guests have arrived? ")
guests = int(guestsStr)
 
withinLimits = guests <= capacity
print("Within limits?", withinLimits)
Sample run
...venue capacity: 150
...guests arrived? 162
Within limits? False
The key line
guests <= capacity is a question. Python 
answers True or False, and you can store that 
answer in a variable like any other value.

Problem 4: What Day Will You Return?
Days are numbered 0 to 6, where 0 is Sunday. Leave on day 3, stay 10 nights — you return on day 6.
startDayStr = input("What day number do you leave? " )
startDay = int(startDayStr)
 
numDaysStr = input("How many days will you stay? " )
numDays = int(numDaysStr)
 
returnDay = (startDay + numDays) % 7
print("You will return on day", returnDay)
Sample run
...day do you leave? 3
...will you stay? 10
You will return on day 6
Why % 7 works
3 + 10 = 13. The week only has 7 days, so 13 % 7 
= 6. Modulo wraps you back around.

Problem 5: Area of a Rectangle
Same program, written more compactly — casting inside input, and the calculation inside print.
# rectangle
length = float(input("Enter rectangle length: "))
width = float(input("Enter rectangle width: "))
 
print("The area is:", length * width)
Sample run
...rectangle length: 8
...rectangle width: 4.5
The area is: 36.0
Two styles, same result
Problems 1–4 used a separate line for each step. 
This one folds them together . Both are correct — 
the step-by-step version is easier to debug when 
something goes wrong.

Problem 6: Even or Odd?
Print True if the integer is even, False if it is odd. Still no if statement.
# another Boolean expression, using %
num = int(input("Enter an integer: "))
 
even = num % 2 == 0
print("Is it even?", even)
Sample run
Enter an integer: 7
Is it even? False

Problem 7: Accumulating a Total
Start a total at 0, add three numbers to it one at a time, then print the total and the average.
total = 0
 
num1 = int(input("Enter num1: "))
total = total + num1
 
num2 = int(input("Enter num2: "))
total = total + num2
 
num3 = int(input("Enter num3: "))
total = total + num3
 
print("The total is:", total)
print("The average is:", round(total / 3, 2))
Sample run
Enter num1: 10
Enter num2: 15
Enter num3: 20
The total is: 45
The average is: 15.0
total = total + num1 is not algebra. It means: 
work out the right side, then store that answer 
back in total.

Before the Assignment
The Str naming convention Read into nameStr , cast, store as name. Use it every time.
Cast before you calculate input() gives text. Text does not do arithmetic.
Booleans instead of if statements A comparison is a value. Store it, print it.
/ versus // versus % Decimal, whole part, remainder . Know which one you need.
math.ceil and math.floor Always up, always down. You will need both.
Retype these programs yourself this week. Reading code is not the same as writing it.
